QuestionStmt.S: Calculate vapour pressure of pure volatile liquid $B$ at given temperature if mole fraction of liquid $B$ and vapour pressure of pure volatile liquid $A$ are 0.4 and 400 mm Hg respectively. $[P_{\text{total}} = 600 \text{ mmHg}]$

Solution.S:
There are two volatile liquids A and B.

Using Dalton's law of partial pressure:
$$P_{\text{total}} = P_A + P_B$$

Applying Raoult's law:
$$P_{\text{total}} = x_A P_A^0 + x_B P_B^0$$

Given: $x_B = 0.4$, so $x_A = 1 - x_B = 0.6$.

$P_A^0 = 400$ mm Hg, $P_{\text{total}} = 600$ mm Hg.

$$600 = 0.6 \times 400 + 0.4 \times P_B^0$$

$$600 = 240 + 0.4 \times P_B^0$$

$$0.4 \times P_B^0 = 360$$

$$P_B^0 = \frac{360}{0.4} = 900 \text{ mm Hg}$$

Thus vapour pressure of pure B is 900 mm Hg, which corresponds to option D.
